title: Cubical boundary, coordinate projections and translation structure
statement:
Let $r\geq0$ be an integer, $D=\mathbf Z^r$, and $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ its ordered standard basis. For $0\leq a\leq r$ let $C_a$ be the free abelian group [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on $[v,I]$ with $v\in D$, $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and $|I|=a$, and set $C_a=0$ in all other integer degrees. Put $q_i(I)=\#\{j\in I:j<i\}$ and define homomorphisms by
$$\partial_a[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{q_i(I)}([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}])\quad(a\geq1),\qquad \partial_a=0\quad(a\leq0).$$
For $1\leq i\leq r$ set $\rho_i(v)=v-v_i u_i$ and define $p_{i,a}:C_a\to C_a$ by $p_{i,a}[v,I]=0$ when $i\in I$ and $p_{i,a}[v,I]=[\rho_i(v),I]$ otherwise, with zero maps outside the range. Let $\epsilon:C_0\to\mathbf Z$ send every vertex to $1$ and $s:\mathbf Z\to C_0$ send $1$ to $[0,\varnothing]$. Then $\partial_{a-1}\partial_a=0$ in every integer degree and $\epsilon\partial_1=0$, so $C_\bullet$ is an augmented chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For every $i,j,a$,
$$\partial_a p_{i,a}=p_{i,a-1}\partial_a,\qquad p_{i,a}p_{j,a}=p_{j,a}p_{i,a}.$$
Put $P_{0,a}=1$ and $P_{k,a}=p_{1,a}\cdots p_{k,a}$ for $1\leq k\leq r$. Then $P_{r,0}=s\epsilon$ and $P_{r,a}=0$ for $a\ne0$ (the empty product for $r=0$ included). For $w\in D$ let $\tau_{w,a}[v,I]=[v+w,I]$. Then $\partial_a\tau_{w,a}=\tau_{w,a-1}\partial_a$ and $\epsilon\tau_{w,0}=\epsilon$. If $\mathcal I_a$ is the finite set of subsets of size $a$, there is a basis-preserving isomorphism
$$C_a\cong\bigoplus_{I\in\mathcal I_a}\mathbf Z^{(D)},\qquad [v,I]\longmapsto\text{the basis vector at }v\text{ in summand }I,$$
where $\mathbf Z^{(D)}$ denotes the free abelian group on $D$. The isomorphism intertwines translation with the regular action $w[v]=[v+w]$ on each summand. Thus these summands are copies of the free integral $D$-module on one orbit. For $r=0$, $C_0\cong\mathbf Z$ by $[0,\varnothing]\mapsto1$, with $\epsilon=s=1$ under this identification.

proof.text: Every element of $C_a$ has a unique finitely supported expression $\sum_{v,I}n_{v,I}[v,I]$ by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Extend each prescribed basis map $f$ by $f(\sum n_{v,I}[v,I])=\sum n_{v,I}f[v,I]$. Each boundary image has at most $r$ signed differences, hence at most $2r$ basis terms. These formulas are well-defined homomorphisms: addition adds coefficients and multiplication by an integer multiplies every coefficient, so they are $\mathbf Z$-linear. The same construction gives $\epsilon$ and $s$. In degrees with zero group use the unique zero maps. Equality of these maps is checked on the basis by the finite-sum formula.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; agent-written verification on the displayed lattice basis.

proof.text: For $2\le a\le r$, expand $\partial_{a-1}\partial_a[v,I]$ and pair the two orders of deleting distinct $i<j$ in $I$. Put $J=I\setminus\{i,j\}$. Both orders have the same unsigned expression $[v+u_i+u_j,J]-[v+u_i,J]-[v+u_j,J]+[v,J]$. Deleting $i$ then $j$ has exponent $q_i(I)+q_j(I)-1$, whereas deleting $j$ then $i$ has exponent $q_j(I)+q_i(I)$. Their signs are opposite. Every term belongs to exactly one such pair, so the sum is zero. For $a=1$ or $a\le0$ a differential is zero; for $a>r$ the domain is zero. This proves the identity in all integer degrees.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; agent-written verification on the displayed lattice basis.

proof.text: On a degree-one generator, $\epsilon\partial_1[v,\{i\}]=\epsilon([v+u_i,\varnothing]-[v,\varnothing])=1-1=0$. The preceding square-zero identity is exactly the chain-complex condition of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. The homomorphism $\epsilon$ is its augmentation because it annihilates $\partial_1$, and $\epsilon s(1)=1$. No exactness assertion is needed here.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; agent-written verification on the displayed lattice basis.

proof.text:
Fix $i$ and a basis cell $[v,I]$ of positive degree. If $i
otin I$, every $j\in I$ satisfies $j
e i$, hence $ho_i(v+u_j)=ho_i(v)+u_j$; the signs and deleted subsets are unchanged, giving $\partial_a p_{i,a}[v,I]=p_{i,a-1}\partial_a[v,I]$ term by term. If $i\in I$, the left side is zero. On the right all $j
e i$ terms are killed since their subsets still contain $i$; the remaining $j=i$ term is zero since $ho_i(v+u_i)=ho_i(v)$. In degree zero both sides vanish, and outside the range their domain is zero. Thus these families are chain maps in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: For a fixed $I$, either $i\in I$ or $j\in I$, in which case both composites $p_{i,a}p_{j,a}$ and $p_{j,a}p_{i,a}$ kill $[v,I]$, or both indices are absent. In the latter case the two maps reset those coordinates, in either order; $\rho_i\rho_j(v)=\rho_j\rho_i(v)$, including $i=j$. Hence the projections commute. More explicitly $P_{k,a}[v,I]$ is zero if $I\cap\{1,\ldots,k\}\ne\varnothing$, and otherwise is $[v-\sum_{j=1}^k v_j u_j,I]$, by successive application of the definitions. With $k=r$ this is $[0,\varnothing]$ for a vertex and zero for positive-degree cells. It equals $s\epsilon$ in degree zero; in negative degrees both the group and its endomorphism are zero.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; agent-written verification on the displayed lattice basis.

proof.text: Translations satisfy $\tau_{w,a}\tau_{z,a}[v,I]=[v+z+w,I]=\tau_{w+z,a}[v,I]$ and $\tau_{0,a}=1$. For each boundary summand, $(v+w)+u_i=(v+u_i)+w$ and the subset and sign are unchanged. Therefore $\partial_a\tau_{w,a}=\tau_{w,a-1}\partial_a$ on every generator, with the zero-degree cases immediate. Also $\epsilon\tau_{w,0}[v,\varnothing]=1=\epsilon[v,\varnothing]$, giving the augmentation equivariance for the trivial action on $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; agent-written verification on the displayed lattice basis.

proof.text: The set $\mathcal I_a$ is finite since it is contained in the powerset of the $r$-element coordinate set (and is empty outside $0\le a\le r$). Send $\sum_{v,I}n_{v,I}[v,I]$ to the tuple whose $I$-component is $\sum_v n_{v,I}[v]$. Each sum has finite support. Conversely send a tuple of finitely supported sums $\bigl(\sum_v m_{I,v}[v]\bigr)_I$ to $\sum_{I,v}m_{I,v}[v,I]$. These are homomorphisms by addition of coefficients, and their two composites fix all coefficients, so they give the stated basis-preserving isomorphism using [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. On the basis it sends $\tau_w[v,I]$ to $[v+w]$ in the same summand. That summand has one free orbit of basis elements: $w[0]=[w]$ and the equation $w[0]=[0]$ forces $w=0$. Thus it is the free integral $D$-module on one orbit, with the asserted regular action.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; agent-written verification on the displayed lattice basis.

proof.text: For $r=0$, the group $D=\mathbf Z^0$ has just its zero element and the only subset is $\varnothing$. Thus $C_0$ consists uniquely of the multiples $n[0,\varnothing]$. The maps $n[0,\varnothing]\mapsto n$ and $n\mapsto n[0,\varnothing]$ are inverse; these are $\epsilon$ and $s$. All other groups vanish. The empty product $P_{0,0}=1$ is consequently $s\epsilon$, and $P_{0,a}=1_{0}=0$ for $a\ne0$. The empty set of projection indices requires no further case.
